summary: Takeshi Fujii is an Indologist and historian who studied at the Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Delhi. He served at the Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from 1987 as assistant, becoming professor and emeritus professor in 2021.

Takeshi Hasegawa works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a lecturing post at Ryukoku University (attested 1998) and lecturer posts at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Takeshi Karashima was a Sinologist who studied at Yamaguchi Higher School and Tokyo Imperial University (~1924–1927). His career included positions at Keijo Imperial University (~1932–1945), Kamakura's library (~1949–1952), Sagami Women's University (~1952–1967), and Showa Women's University.

Takeshi Umehara worked in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies, studying at Kyoto University under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He held posts at Ryukoku University, Ritsumeikan University, Kyoto City University of Arts, and served as director of Nichibunken (1987–1995).

Takeshiro Kuraishi was a Sinologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1918–1921). He served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1939–1949), taught at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1958), and chaired the Chugokugo Gakkai (~1956–1975).

Takezo Kaneko was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji (~1926–1929). He held professorships and posts at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1966), International Christian University (~1966–1976), Seikei University (~1976–1980), and Hokkaido University.

Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé. He succeeded Trulshik Rinpoche Ngawang Chökyi Lodrö in 2012, serving as Supreme Head of the Nyingma (~2012–2015).

Taku Fukuda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hajime Sakurabe. He was appointed full-time lecturer at Doho University in 1995 and is attested in 2026 as a Doho University professor and Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute affiliate.

Takudo Ishikawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He was a research fellow at the Jodo Shu Research Institute (attested 2005–2006) and has held teaching posts at Taisho University (attested 2015 and 2026).

Takushu Sugimoto is an Indologist, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his degrees at Tohoku University. He was a professor at Kanazawa University (~1986–1999; emeritus ~1999), Komazawa University (attested 1990), and Kinjo University (attested 2004).
Tamara Cohen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned her PhD at the University of Toronto in 2023 under the supervision of Srilata Raman and Jürgen Hanneder.

Tampalawela Dhammaratana is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Kelaniya, the University of Paris under Jean-François Lyotard, Paris-Sorbonne University under Michel Hulin, and completed postdoctoral studies at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat.

Tan Chung is a historian and Sinologist who earned his PhD at Visva-Bharati University. He served as professor at the University of Delhi (~1964–1978) and head of Chinese and Japanese studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1978–1994).
Tan Poh Beng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam.
Tan Sitong was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Renshan Yang between ~1896 and 1898, as well as under Wang Zhengyi.

Tan Yun-shan was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied at Hunan Normal University and Chuanshan Academy. He founded the Sino-Indian Cultural Society and served as Professor of Chinese Studies at Visva-Bharati University (~1937–1968).
Tanaya Afroz is a linguist who pursued doctoral research under Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya and has been affiliated with The Asiatic Society as a research scholar and fellow (attested 2026).
Tandin Dorji is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Tibetology who has worked as a lecturer at the National Institute of Education in Paro and as a history lecturer at Sherubtse College.

Tanero Sasakawa was a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He completed his studies at the University of Tokyo (~1892–1896) and later held posts at Toyo University and Meiji University.

Tansen Sen is a historian and Sinologist who studied at Peking University and the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair. He taught history at Baruch College (1997–2017) before becoming a professor at NYU Shanghai in 2017.
